title: Improve CSS scoping for older browsers
description:
Follow up from https://github.com/rstudio/r2d3/pull/27, mostly to improve support in RStudio 1.1:

1. RStudio 1.1 was triggering errors in the console. This was due to `Set` not available in JavaScript.
2. RStudio 1.1 was not triggering resize for the widgets, this was due to we components.js not fully loading and is now fixed.

That said, this change does not enable the polyfill in RStudio 1.1, this is fine for the most part since RStudio uses iFrames in most cases (viewer, notebooks, etc) so the CSS is correctly scoped. However,  flexdashboard preview and other cases that host multiple widgets won't properly scope the CSS until the document is opened in the web browser.

title: Clean up javascript library paths
description:
Follow up on https://github.com/rstudio/r2d3/pull/27#pullrequestreview-120154005.

Looks like [leaflet/inst/htmlwidgets/lib](https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/tree/master/inst/htmlwidgets/lib), [dygraphs/inst/htmlwidgets/lib](https://github.com/rstudio/dygraphs/tree/master/inst/htmlwidgets/lib) and [plotly/inst/htmlwidgets/lib](https://github.com/ropensci/plotly/tree/master/inst/htmlwidgets/lib) all keep their libraries under `inst/htmlwidgets/lib`, at least for consistency, would make sense to follow a similar convention in `r2d3` as well.

This PR changes the libraries location to:

```
inst/htmlwidgets/lib/d3
inst/htmlwidgets/lib/d3-jetpack
inst/htmlwidgets/lib/r2d3
inst/htmlwidgets/lib/webcomponents
```

title: CSS Scoping with Shadow DOM
description: Adds support for CSS scoping to fix #23 using Shadow DOM and webcomponents pollyfill. With this change, global styles defined not specified as dependencies in R2D3 won't affect the D3 rendering. For instance, without this change, the following rmarkdown document renders as follows:: `````` ```css /* ~/RStudio/global-style.css */ rect { stroke-width: 2px; stroke: steelblue; } ``` `````` `````` --- output: html_document: css: ~/RStudio/global-style.css --- ```{r setup} library(r2d3) ``` ```{d3 data=c(0.3, 0.6, 0.8, 0.95, 0.40, 0.20)} var barHeight = Math.ceil(height / data.length); svg.selectAll('rect') .data(data) .enter().append('rect') .attr('width', function(d) { return d * width; }) .attr('height', barHeight) .attr('y', function(d, i) { return i * barHeight; }) .attr('fill', '#EEEEFF'); ``` `````` with this change, the style is isolated and the document renders without the global style influencing D3: Here is how the DOM looks like: ## Alternate Approaches It was discussed in https://github.com/rstudio/r2d3/pull/24 to consider: 1. Shadow DOM 2. Scoped styles 3. Parsing CSS and then inject our own unique ID. For (3), found out https://github.com/tabatkins/parse-css is a descent approach; however, this library currently does not support generating the CSS back form the AST. I explored using SASS with https://github.com/medialize/sass.js/ since we could have created a nested style for each widget; however, their JS file is several MBs in size since it's optimized for compilation, not online rendering. Option (2), as discussed, it's already deprecated by most browsers so I prioritized (1) as a longer term solution. For (1), validated the pollyfill works correctly on firefox which does not yet support the Shadow DOM, worth mentioning that the pollyfill is 100Kb.

title: Adds D3 to Shiny communication vignette
qualify css with r2d3 class
description:
@javierluraschi This is the beginnings of addressing issue #23 however after thinking about it further I don't think it's enough.

Here we basically qualify all CSS references with `.r2d3`, which ensures that they don't leak out beyond r2d3 visualizations. However, this doesn't prevent the CSS from various r2d3 scripts affecting eachother, which means that it in some cases it will be impossible to compose a page or app that has 2 different r2d3 visualizations.

Some ways to overcome this:

1) We really want something like a shadow DOM however SVG doesn't support this: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40810372/augmenting-svg-tag-with-shadow-dom

2) We could use a scoped styles polyfill like this one: https://github.com/thomaspark/scoper (or do our own version of this). Note that scoped styles have been removed from the HTML spec (likely in favor of the shadow DOM) but some browsers still support them natively. If we go this route we should probably research various available solutions and see which one is best.

3) We could parse the CSS and then inject our own unique ID. This parsing could actually be done on the client in JS w/ something like this: https://github.com/tabatkins/parse-css. Note that it is possible for us to know/control the element ID by passing `elementID` to `createWidget` (we'd just have to our own random/unique element ID implementation).

This PR is a placeholder for this work (my guess is that if take one of the above approaches then we'll get rid of the `.r2d3` prefixing b/c it will no longer be necessary.

title: built-in support for d3-jetpack extension
description:
This PR adds an `extensions` argument to `html_dependencies_d3()` and implements support for `d3-jetpack` as a standard extension. This is provided as an enhancement to the `dependencies` argument (which can already accommodate d3-jetpack) for 2 reasons:

1) We expect that the `html_dependencies_d3()` function will be used by htmlwidget package authors that wish to incorporate later versions of d3 (e.g. v4 or v5) within reports or applications that already include d3 v3 (e.g. via widespread usage of d3 v3 in existing htmlwidgets). Since this mechanism works by renaming the global instance of d3 to `d3v4` or `d3v5`, d3 extensions actually require special modification to correctly add themselves to `d3v4` or `d3v5`. This change embeds a modified copy of d3-jetpack which works with `d3v4` or `d3v5`.

2) While including a filesystem reference to "d3-jetpack.js" within `dependencies` works fine today, this does create a burden of copying that file into the directory of every d3 visualization (and then maintaining it when d3-jetpack is updated) and also creates a separate embedded copy of d3-jetpack (15K) for each visualization. This change allows us to share a common instance of d3-jetpack both on the filesystem and within pages/apps.

We can consider adding support for other commonly used d3 extensions, but note that since many extensions are of uneven quality and/or not actively maintained *and* there is already a workaround for these (copy the file and add it to `dependencies`) we should be pretty conservative about adding new standard extensions.

cc @javierluraschi @nstrayer @timelyportfolio @jcheng5

title: Allow non data-frames to pass data asis
description:
Previous commit https://github.com/rstudio/r2d3/commit/9f522211d328be41877ffd6942bf49a2a7f2d1c1#diff-e446088a017e6c3093395c7f863509caR21 added conversion to data frame but this is not strictly required. We do make use of [HTMLWidgets.dataframeToD3()](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/htmlwidgets/vignettes/develop_advanced.html#htmlwidgets.dataframetod3) but only for data frames, if users pass different format, they would have to adjust their D3 script to support the data they pass appropriately.

In the future, we could consider making more automatic conversions, but at this point, it is not clear to me what conversions would be helpful.
